setting: A fictional support call about a broken home internet connection.

presentation.situation: Your home internet has not worked since {{since}}. You call {{name}} at support. You have already {{tried}}. Explain the problem and check you understand the solution.
presentation.opening: Thanks for contacting support, this is {{name}}. What problem are you experiencing?

brief.you_are: You are a customer calling internet support.
brief.situation: Your home internet has not worked since {{since}}. You call {{name}} at support. You have already {{tried}}. Explain the problem and check you understand the solution.
brief.task: Say exactly what is wrong, say what you have already tried, and confirm the solution.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} understands the problem, and you can repeat what to do next.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are a customer calling internet support.
goals: Say exactly what is wrong, say what you have already tried, and confirm the solution.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: Answers calls for the internet provider

card.want: To find the real problem quickly, without repeating steps you already tried.
card.speech: Clear, polite support language. Explains one step at a time.
tactics: Ask what the lights on the router show
Ask them to repeat the fix

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: A technician visit would take two working days, if the fix does not work.

objectives.evidence: The learner states the problem specifically.
alternatives: The problem is that my internet stopped working last night.

objectives.evidence: The learner says what they already tried.
The learner confirms the solution in their own words.
alternatives: So I should reset it and wait, is that correct?

beats.goal: Find out precisely what is wrong.
opportunity: Can you tell me what exactly stopped working?
What happens when you try to connect?
beats.orient: You called me because your internet is broken. Tell me what is wrong. Start with: The problem is.
fallback: What happens when you try to connect?
Can you tell me what exactly stopped working?

beats.goal: Find out what has been tried.
opportunity: What have you done so far?
beats.orient: Tell me what you already tried. Use: I have tried, or: I already.
fallback: What have you done so far?

beats.goal: Check that the solution is understood.
signals: \b(?:so i should|is that correct|do you mean|that should)\b
opportunity: The next step is {{fix}}. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me what you are going to do?
beats.orient: I told you the next step. Now say it back to me. Start with: So I should.
fallback: Can you tell me what you are going to do?
The next step is {{fix}}. Does that make sense?

closing_line: That's right. Thanks for calling, and I hope that solves it.

o1.good: A precise description saves time for both of you.
o1.micro_lesson: Say what, since when, and what you see.
o1.model: The problem is that my internet stopped working last night.

o2.good: Using the present perfect for what you have done so far.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: I've tried, or: I have already.

o3.good: Saying back the solution avoids a second call.
o3.micro_lesson: Say: So I should, then ask: Is that correct?
o3.model: So I should reset it and wait two minutes, is that correct?

variants.name: Farah
variants.fix: a full reset using the small button on the back

variants.name: Ben
variants.tried: checked that the cable is plugged in
variants.fix: a new settings update, sent from the support system
